8b987812ef6b4eea: The Pi coding agent reached its 1.0 milestone on Thursday while being treated for whiplash. One of the core new inclusions is support for Model Context Protocol (MCP), which Pi creator Mario Zechner once dismissed as unnecessary. Earendil, the company formed by Armin Ronacher and Colin Daymond Hanna that acquired Pi in April 2026, explained the about-face by noting that things change. Not only has MCP improved, the biz said, but changes the Pi devs implemented in MCP have made integrating other capabilities easier. "For example, the changes we have made to MCP also enable the use of Jev more easily within Pi," the company said, in reference to the widely noted Jev decision model that has already elicited imitations. "Ultimately what Pi needs is quite similar to what MCP needs: a sandbox to play with in the form of an interpreter." Earendil describes Pi as "a hardened, minimal, extensible agent harness that you can make your own." If Pi were a Python web framework, it would be Flask rather than Django. Nonetheless, Pi has gained some features. These include Codemode, a harness-side sandbox that helps agents issue tool calls, with support for MCP, decision models, and image models; extension support for virtual models; deferred tool loading; cache warming for Anthropic models; mid-conversation system messages; a new TUI theme; and full-screen mode by default. Alongside these features, Earendil has built Pi Durable, described as "a new substrate for building long-running agentic applications." It's a distinct component from Pi, the company explained, in order to preserve Pi's minimalist design. The Pi agent connects the underlying model to tools to manage conversation; Pi Durable represents the layer that orchestrates multiple conversations and handles the storage backend, via SQLite and JSONL. "Pi Durable is that harness," the company explains. "It does not replace the Pi coding agent. It is a framework for building any agentic application, coding agents included. It shares not only code with the Pi coding agent, like pi-ai, but also its principles: minimalism and malleability." ®
5115e2c8d83752b9: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Lee Chean Chung had stopped attending PKR meetings and party activities for more than a year before resigning as the Petaling Jaya member of Parliament today.
The PKR president said Lee had also been absent from the party's congress, indicating that the lawmaker had long distanced himself from the party's affairs.
"Oh, he stopped a long time ago. You only found out now? He had not attended party meetings for a long time, and he did not attend the congress either.
"So it is appropriate. If he is no longer interested, there is no problem. Go in a good way.
"Thank you for his contributions all this while," he said.
7e4b82d49e6d7b7d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The Batu flood retention pond could be upgraded into a dual-purpose facility that retains its flood mitigation role while providing up to 10 million litres of alternative water supply daily.

The Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry (Petra) said the proposed pilot project would provide five million litres per day (MLD) for domestic use, potentially benefiting about 6,000 homes, and another 5 MLD for industrial use in the Batu area.

Previous studies found that the pond has the potential for water abstraction of up to 95 MLD. However, Petra said an initial capacity of 10 MLD had been proposed to assess the feasibility of the dual-purpose concept.
“The proposal remains subject to confirmation through a feasibility study and concept design currently being undertaken by the National Water Research Institute of Malaysia (Nahrim).

“The pilot project will be implemented in two phases, with Phase One involving the feasibility study and concept design, expected to be completed this December, while Phase Two will involve physical implementation based on the study’s findings and subject to government approval,” the ministry said in a statement.
Petra stressed that flood mitigation would remain the pond’s primary function.
The ongoing study will assess the technical requirements to ensure its use as an alternative water source does not compromise its existing flood mitigation capacity.
It will also examine raw water quality, pollution levels and treatability to determine whether the water is suitable as an alternative supply source.
Petra said the project was in line with the National Water Policy’s aim of strengthening water security through more efficient, sustainable and resilient water resource management.
It would also enhance the country’s preparedness for the impact of climate change and extreme weather, including floods and droughts. — Bernama
89a07bcbf8ce68cf: KUALA LUMPUR: Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah has assured Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim that his government will provide full cooperation to determine the status of 55 Malaysians missing following the disaster in Nepal.
Anwar said he spoke with Shah, who agreed to facilitate efforts to help the families of those missing obtain certainty as soon as possible.
"I have had conversations with the prime minister. He is willing to give all the cooperation.
"We have asked the Attorney-General to follow through.

"They have their laws, our laws too. The strict (period is) six or seven years, they have three. But we can still apply to the courts, and he assured me that he will give all the cooperation necessary to facilitate so that the families can get the results as soon as possible," he said.
58aa4674fbd69819: REMBAU: Canadian cyclist Riley Pickrell timed his late surge to perfection, winning Stage 6 of Le Tour de Langkawi (LTdL) from Pandan Indah to Rembau in a tight sprint finish today.
The Modern Adventure Pro Cycling rider completed the 121.3km route in two hours, 40 minutes, and six seconds, narrowly beating XDS Astana's Matteo Malucelli on the line.
Seppe Van den Boer of Tudor Pro Cycling crossed the line in third, while Rory Townsend (Unibet Rose Rockets) and Christian Rees (Team Picnic PostNL) rounded out the top five.
Pickrell credited his team's tactics for the win, especially Scott McGill, who set up his decisive sprint through the final corner.
"We knew we needed to be in a very good position and were hoping Scott could lead me right up to the corner.
"He put in an incredible effort, taking me right through the turn and providing a brilliant lead-out to the finish line," he said.
Pickrell revealed the team's race plan began early in the stage when teammate Kieran Haug joined an initial break-away to force rivals into a costly pursuit.
"Kieran joined the early break, forcing Astana to burn energy as early as the 10th or 15th kilometre.
"Meanwhile, the rest of us could rest and conserve energy in the peloton. It was all down to Kieran's effort," he said.
The victory marked a key milestone for Pickrell, who claimed stage wins at the Tour of Sibiu in 2024 and 2025.

"I started this season aiming for a win. I've recorded professional victories every year for the past four years, and with the season drawing to a close, I was really hungry for this result. I knew my time would come," he said.
He also acknowledged the challenge posed by Malucelli following several close sprint finishes earlier in the tour.
"I have tremendous respect for Malucelli. Without him here, this victory wouldn't mean as much. He is a phenomenal sprinter and someone I look up to, so I'm thrilled to get this win," he said.
In the overall standings, Tudor Pro Cycling's Lennart Jasch retained the Orange Jersey as general classification leader after six stages with a total time of 21:38:39.
He holds a 42-second cushion over Jan Castellon (Caja Rural-Seguros RGA), with Jose Manuel Diaz (Burgos Burpellet BH) a further 38 seconds back in third.
Jasch also maintained his lead in the King of the Mountains classification (Polka Dot Jersey) with 45 points, ahead of Petr Rikunov (Wheeltop Rotor Chengdu Team) on 41 points and Castellon on 26.
In the Sprint classification (Blue Jersey), Malucelli leads with 44 points, holding a five-point advantage over Pickrell (39 points), while Van den Boer sits third on 20 points.

In the Best Asian classification (White Jersey), Aisan Racing Team's Yuhi Todome leads in 21:46:00, followed by St George Continental Team's Tsen Ren Bao (21:49:44), with younger brother Tsen Ren Han — riding for the Malaysian national team — in third (21:51:25).
Stage 7 today covers 158.9km from Melaka to Batu Pahat, featuring three intermediate sprint points at Tangkak, Bukit Kepong, and Parit Sulong.

d90442d871e08531: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia survived an early fright before overcoming Hong Kong 2-1 to retain their Asian Games women's squash team title in Nagoya today.
The victory earned Malaysia their seventh gold medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Games, surpassing their target of six gold medals.
Aifa Azman put Malaysia ahead by defeating Tomato Ho 11-9, 11-9, 12-10 in the opening match.

Hong Kong then gave Malaysia a scare when Chan Sin Yuk upset world No. 5 S. Subramaniam 11-7, 9-11, 9-11, 11-5, 11-7 to level the tie. However, Aifa's younger sister, Aira Azman, secured the winning point and the gold medal by defeating Lee Ka Yi 11-9, 11-5, 11-4 in the deciding match.
Malaysia had also defeated Hong Kong 2-1 to capture the team gold at Hangzhou 2022.
Sivasangari is set to receive an incentive of RM100,000 for her efforts, comprising RM80,000 for the individual event and RM20,000 for the team event.
fb5b132a2e810892: KUALA LUMPUR: Former national coach Stephen van Huizen believes the Asian Games final on Saturday against India is a chance to create history by winning the gold for the first time.

Stephen coached the national team to the final twice at the Asian Games in Guangzhou in 2010 and Indonesia in 2018 and on both occasions Malaysia lost in the final to Pakistan and Japan, respectively.
Now, Malaysia can automatically qualify for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, ending a 28-year wait.

"India start as favourites based on their ranking and so the pressure is on them to win the gold medal. The Malaysian team played according to our ranking and took one game at a time and performed well as a unit in the tournament.
"When the team needed to fight through tough moments, for example against Pakistan, they have shown resilience and dug deep to find a win over the Green Shirts 5-4 in the group stage.
"And that helped set up a semi-final against South Korea, which Malaysia won 2-1. As underdogs, we should approach the finals without feeling any pressure, as we have done well to reach the final.
"My advice to the players is to be disciplined and to follow the game plans and tactics of the coach. Stay focused and fight every minute and take whatever chances that come our way.
"As this is the last game of the tournament, do not hold anything back, give your best and enjoy the occasion.
"In a final, anything is possible. We have to be prepared for any eventualities because we have nothing to lose.
"We should see it as an opportunity to create history by winning gold for the first time and automatically qualify for the Olympics.

"I can't imagine any bigger motivation for the players to give their best. Some of the players have been through this before so draw on your experience to help the younger players to approach the finals with confidence," said Stephen.
Malaysia will be relying on experienced forwards like Faizal Saari and Azrai Aizad Abu Kamal, who have each scored nine goals in six matches.
Faizal is an experienced player who will be playing his third Asian Games final and he needs to break through India's defence marshalled by captain Harmanpreet Singh to score.
Harmanpreet is also deadly with penalty corners as he converted 10 in six matches.
Goalkeeper Zaimi Mat Deris must be on his toes between the posts as India have skilful forwards like Abhishek, Dilpreet Singh and Sukhjeet Singh, who scored 24 goals in Nagoya.
7e04127c1cdd1a13: GEORGE TOWN: A 71-year-old eatery worker has been remanded for seven days on suspicion of raping his employer's 18-year-old daughter in a shopping mall toilet.

Magistrate S. Selvaranjini issued the remand order, which runs until next Thursday, to facilitate investigations under Section 376 of the Penal Code for rape and Section 377C of the same law for committing carnal intercourse against the order of nature.
The suspect covered his face while being escorted out of the courtroom by police officers to avoid being photographed by media personnel.
In the incident, which occurred about 4.30pm, the suspect had taken the victim for a walk at a shopping mall along Persiaran Gurney.
While there, he allegedly dragged her into a male toilet on the second floor before forcibly raping and sexually assaulting her.
The assault allegedly continued until another mall visitor knocked on the toilet door.
Following the incident, the suspect allegedly gave the victim cash before taking her back to her father's nearby shop.
Traumatised by the ordeal, the teenager confided in her family, who then lodged a police report, leading to the suspect's arrest.
7d9141256e614467: PUTRAJAYA: A former bowling coach has been sentenced to another two years in prison for outraging the modesty of a former Sukma athlete who was 13 when the offence was committed.
The Court of Appeal unanimously allowed the prosecution’s appeal against the acquittal of Mat Salleh Jalani, 63, under Section 354 of the Penal Code.

The three-member bench, comprising Justices Azmi Ariffin, Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz and Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, ordered the sentence to run consecutively with Mat Salleh’s existing six-year jail term for sexually assaulting another former Sukma athlete under Section 14A of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.
Hayatul, who delivered the judgment, said the High Court had erred in finding that the evidence of the victim, identified as SP3, was not “unusually convincing”.
SP3 was 13 when he began training under Mat Salleh in 2017 in preparation for the 2018 Sukma Games. Mat Salleh drove him to and from training at his mother’s request.
The first incident allegedly occurred in May 2017 at a staff parking area at Coral Crown Bowl in Paya Bunga Square, Kuala Terengganu, with further incidents alleged to have occurred until 2020.
The court noted that two other trainees, SP4 and SP5, claimed they were also molested by Mat Salleh and had witnessed him molesting SP3.
SP3 eventually disclosed the incidents in 2021, saying he did not want other young trainees to suffer what he had experienced.
Hayatul said SP3’s evidence was consistent, remained unshaken under cross-examination, and was supported by his mother and the two trainees.

She said a delay in reporting sexual offences did not, by itself, undermine a victim’s credibility, citing a Federal Court decision recognising that victims may be reluctant to report such incidents for various reasons.
The court restored the conviction imposed by the magistrates’ court and increased the sentence from 18 to 24 months’ jail.
Deputy public prosecutor Ahmad Nazneen Zulkifli appeared for the prosecution, while Fariz Fauzi represented Mat Salleh.
On March 11, another Court of Appeal bench affirmed Mat Salleh’s six-year jail term for sexually assaulting another former Sukma athlete in 2018.

c341f5ff0a906a1f: PUTRAJAYA: State governments have been urged to gazette padi-growing areas to sustain rice cultivation and strengthen food security following a decline in the nation's rice self-sufficiency ratio (SSR).
The rice SSR, which measures the percentage of domestic demand met by local production, fell from 68 per cent in 2018 to 54.3 per cent in 2025.

According to the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry, the proposal was discussed at the second 2026 Agriculture and Food Security Ministers' Meeting with state agriculture executive councillors, chaired by Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu yesterday.

The ministry said shrinking rice cultivation areas contributed to the declining SSR, aligning with a recommendation in the Auditor-General's Report to gazette padi lands to preserve agricultural acreage.
"Malaysia's reliance on imported rice was estimated at 1.416 million metric tonnes, worth RM2.953 billion, in 2025," the ministry said in a statement today.
Agriculture executive councillors from nine states, representatives from state Economic Planning Units, the Finance Ministry, the Economy Ministry, and senior ministry officials attended the meeting.
The meeting discussed measures to protect food-producing areas by zoning them under structure and local plans in accordance with the National Land Use Master Plan.

Proposed steps include the immediate gazetting of 24 state agro-food areas under Permanent Food Production Parks, Permanent Ruminant Production Parks, and Aquaculture Industry Zones, alongside implementing the Livestock Farm Regularisation Scheme and Food Area Protection Mechanism in Sabah and Sarawak.

"These measures support ministry efforts to raise the SSR for strategic commodities while increasing domestic production and strengthening the country's food resilience and security," the statement read.
State governments were also encouraged to participate in Malaysia Fest in Singapore, which has promoted Malaysian agro-food products since 2006.
"Malaysia Fest has shown positive growth, with attendance rising from 75,000 in 2017 to 179,400 in 2025, while sales increased from RM6.59 million to RM15.8 million," the ministry said.

The meeting also reviewed the National Agro-Food Empowerment Programme under the 13th Malaysia Plan, noting that 347 projects worth RM349.15 million were approved out of 782 applications totalling RM2.09 billion received this year.

Delegates examined findings from the 2024 Outcome Evaluation Study of the Land Optimisation Programme, involving 97 projects, 19,447 participants, roughly 40,000 hectares, and RM149.59 million in funding to assess overall effectiveness.

On industry regulation, the meeting acknowledged the drafting of the Fertiliser Bill to establish a transparent framework governing fertiliser quality, distribution, and price stability to safeguard farmers' interests.
7d0ddf479b465331: PETALING JAYA: A larger dividend to the government on the back of elevated oil prices will limit Petroliam Nasional Bhd’s (Petronas) spending on upstream activities and gas infrastructure moving forward, a research house said.

BIMB Securities said the state-owned oil corporation’s capital allocation could come under pressure if the government seeks larger dividend contributions from Petronas to offset higher fuel subsidy costs.

In its Budget 2027 preview note today, the research house said a higher dividend payout could raise questions over Petronas’ longer-term capital allocation including spending on upstream activities, gas infrastructure and energy-transition initiatives.
It said Petronas’ dividend to the government could rise to RM48 billion in 2026 while the government’s fuel subsidy bill could reach RM50 billion, assuming Brent crude averages US$95 a barrel.
Petronas’ dividend to the government stood at RM32 billion in 2025 while the fuel subsidy bill was RM30 billion.

BIMB Securities expects Petronas’ dividend payout to moderate to RM32 billion in 2027 and RM25 billion in 2028, as Brent crude is projected to ease to US$85 a barrel in 2027 and US$75 a barrel in 2028.
In Budget 2026, the Petronas dividend was estimated at RM20 billion for 2026, while total petroleum-related revenue was projected at RM43 billion, or 12.5% of federal revenue.
However, these estimates were made before the onset of the US-Iran war earlier this year, which pushed crude oil prices above US$100 per barrel.

Oil prices have remained elevated despite talks between the US and Iran to end the months-long war. Brent crude has averaged US$92.50 per barrel in the first six months of 2026 and was trading around US$102 today.
BIMB Securities also said higher oil prices may provide only a limited boost to Malaysia’s fiscal position as wider refining margins and resilient fuel demand push up the cost of fuel subsidies.
As oil prices rose, refining margins, or crack spreads, also climbed to more than US$60 a barrel, it noted.
The divergence between crude and refined product prices means subsidy expenditure could rise faster than petroleum-related revenue, it pointed out.
“This could potentially constrain efforts to accelerate fiscal consolidation,” BIMB Securities added.
12491c22f94749d5: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Malaysia’s tourism sector continues to show positive momentum by recording 28.8 million international visitors from January to August this year, a 1.8 per cent increase compared to the same period last year.

Tourism Malaysia deputy director-general (promotion) Mohd Akbal Setia said the positive performance reflects the continued appeal of Malaysia as a tourism destination and the importance of strengthening international tourism partnerships.
“The development is particularly relevant as the country continues to strengthen its industry under the Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 campaign,” he said.

He said this when delivering a speech on behalf of Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing at the opening of the International Tourism, Arts and Culture Exhibition and Conference (INTACT) 2026 at Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre here today.

Mohd Akbal said tourism is an important economic driver contributing over 15 per cent to Malaysia’s gross domestic product (GDP), with its benefits extending across the tourism value chain to support businesses and livelihoods from hotels and e-hailing services to local artisans and family-run restaurants.
Touching on the event, Mohd Akbal said INTACT had garnered strong participation, underscoring the platform’s growing influence and capabilities.

“In only its second edition, INTACT has brought together 154 exhibitors from 35 countries, reflecting the organisers and industry partners’ commitment to establishing this event as an international platform for tourism, arts, and culture sectors,” he said.
He added that the platform is vital for expanding joint promotions and creating new tourism experiences that benefit both destinations and local communities.
Mohd Akbal also encouraged all exhibitors and participants to make full use of the event to establish business connections and explore long-lasting opportunities for collaboration. — Bernama
02ac4c969f22f04d: JOHOR BARU: The marine police crippled a subsidised diesel smuggling operation with the seizure of 23,000 litres of fuel worth RM949,160 in a raid at Jalan Penaga, Taman Kota Puteri, Masai, yesterday.
Region Two Marine Police commander Assistant Commissioner Noor Azman Jamal said a 50-year-old lorry driver was arrested and two lorries were seized during the 11.45am raid.
"Following the arrest of the lorry driver, who is suspected of acting as a distributor for the fuel, we seized three more lorries in the nearby area.
"Further inspection revealed a quantity of diesel stored in compartment tanks at the back of the lorries," he said in a statement today.
Noor Azman said police seized a total of five lorries comprising two green Isuzu lorries, two white Hino lorries, and one green Mitsubishi Fuso lorry.
Also seized were 23,000 litres of diesel fuel, 24 compartment tanks, and two electric pumps with hoses.
"Initial investigations indicate that the suspect had been carrying out the activity for the past two months.
"The case is being investigated under Section 21 of the Control of Supplies Act 1961," he said.
75e73e82a4dc8af6: JERUSALEM: Arab Israeli politician Sami Abu Shehadeh withdrew his candidacy on Thursday from October's parliamentary election after Israel's Supreme Court indicated a majority of its judges supported barring him from the race.

Arab Israeli parties are seen by political analysts as potential kingmakers in the Oct 27 election, with polls showing neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition nor the main opposition bloc on course for a majority.
Abu Shehadeh leads the left-wing Palestinian Balad party and served in the Knesset, Israel's parliament, from 2019 to 2022.
The Balad leader was withdrawing his candidacy, but the decision did not mark the end of his political struggle, his party said in a statement, adding that he would remain the party's leader.
Last week, Israel's Central Elections Committee voted to disqualify Abu Shehadeh at the request of far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir.
The move came after an article in which Abu Shehadeh described Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack as an "important historical event."
He has denied supporting the attack, but the remarks drew sharp criticism.
The Supreme Court convened on Thursday to hear Abu Shehadeh's appeal against the disqualification.
Rather than issue a ruling, the court proposed that he voluntarily withdraw after signalling that most of its judges favoured excluding him from the election.
It gave him until Friday morning to decide.
Abu Shehadeh had little choice but to withdraw in order to avoid a formal disqualification that would have "grave consequences for the country's political and parliamentary life", Balad said.
- 'SEVERE BLOW' -
Disqualifying candidates is rare in Israel, where the Supreme Court has historically overturned most bans approved by the elections committee.

Under Israeli law, candidates can be barred only if they deny Israel's existence as a Jewish and democratic state or support armed struggle by an enemy state or a terrorist organisation against Israel.
Adalah, the Israeli rights group representing Abu Shehadeh, accused the Supreme Court of effectively disqualifying him by pressuring him to withdraw.
"A Palestinian leader has been forced out of the Israeli Knesset elections after the Supreme Court made clear it would remove him," the group said in a statement to AFP.
Adalah said Abu Shehadeh's decades of public life as a human rights activist, legislator and party leader demonstrated his "consistent and unequivocal opposition to violence of any kind."
"It is a severe blow to the right of Palestinian citizens to be represented and to stand for election."
Besides Abu Shehadeh, the elections committee last week barred two Arab electoral lists: the United Arab List and the Joint List, a three-party alliance that includes Balad.
The Supreme Court is due to continue hearing appeals from those parties on Friday.
Arab Israelis, also known as Palestinian citizens of Israel, account for about 20 percent of the country's population. Most identify as Palestinians.
They are descendants of Palestinians who remained within Israel's borders after the state's creation in 1948 and have long complained of discrimination compared with Israel's Jewish majority.--AFP

eef1e9c6b0bc9d34: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is reviewing AI-manipulated footage of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad grieving the death of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, which has circulated on social media.

In a statement today, MCMC said it views the manipulation of actual footage seriously, as it misleads the public, distorts the context of an event, and tarnishes the dignity of individuals and their families.
It added that such acts should not be taken lightly, especially when involving a person's moment of loss and grief.
"MCMC has contacted the relevant social media platforms and is reviewing the content.
"If the review reveals any breach of the law, appropriate action can be taken based on existing legal provisions, including the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588)," the statement read.
MCMC reminded all parties not to create, upload, or spread manipulated content that could mislead the public or harm others.
The commission urged the public to verify the authenticity of content before sharing and to report suspected manipulated materials to social media platforms or relevant authorities.
MCMC stressed that while AI technology offers various benefits to society, its use must come with responsibility.
"Technology should not be used to distort the truth or exploit someone's grief at the expense of human dignity and values," it said.
bb8f93c04103e76f: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court today issued an arrest warrant for an accused in the 2022 abduction of a Palestinian man after he failed to appear for pre-trial case management.

Judge Datuk Mohd Arief Emran Arifin issued the warrant against Muhammad Iqmal Abdul Rahis, 31, the seventh of eight accused, after allowing an application by deputy public prosecutor Zaileen Nadia Zubir.
During the proceedings, Zaileen told the court that Iqmal had been uncontactable since Sept 11 and that his bailor had lodged a police report.
The judge then asked the bailor to explain the situation.
She told the court that she had gone to Iqmal's house to look for him but was unable to locate him.
"I also went to his village in Tanjung Sepat, Kuala Langat, in Selangor and even searched a nearby oil palm plantation.
"However, even his siblings did not know his whereabouts.
"That prompted me to lodge a police report on his disappearance," she said.
Zaileen also said police had gone to Tanjung Sepat to interview Iqmal's parents about his whereabouts.
"Police investigations showed that his father said his son had not returned to the village since January. Efforts to trace him are still ongoing," she said.
In addition to issuing the arrest warrant, Arief Emran ordered the RM50,000 bail to be returned to the bailor after hearing that she had made efforts to locate Iqmal.
Iqmal was represented by lawyer Goh Cia Yee.
The other seven accused, who are out on bail, were present in court today.
They are Tengku Arif Bongsu Tengku Hamid, 45; Mohamad Naziree Mustapha, 45; Faizull Hardey Mohd Isa, 46; Mohd Zaidi Mohd Zain, 60; Nidarahayu Zainal, 40; Raibafie Amdan, 45; and Edy Ko'im Said, 46.
The court had previously fixed the trial for Oct 12 to 15, Oct 19 to 23, and Oct 26 to 29.

In October 2022, 13 men and a woman were charged at the magistrate's court here with abducting Palestinian Omar ZM Albelbaisy Raeda, 35, allegedly to obtain a reward in the form of information relating to software used to hack mobile phones.

They were Edy Ko'im, 45; Mohamad Norakmal Hassan, 46; Dody Junaidi, 47; Tengku Arif Bongsu Tengku Hamid, 44; Mohamad Naziree Mustapha, 44; Faizull Hardey Mohd Isa, 45; Muhammad Iqmal, 30; Mohamad Sufian Saly, 28; Muhammad Al Hatim; Nidarahayu Zainal, 39; Raibafie Amdan, 44; Mohd Zaidi Mohd Zain, 59; Mohd Azwan Jamaludin, 42; and Tengku Hazarul Ismail Tengku Hamid, 54.
They were charged with committing the offence at Jalan Mayang here about 10.40pm on Sept 28, 2022.
The charge was framed under Section 3 of the Kidnapping Act 1961, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which carries a jail term of between 30 and 40 years and whipping upon conviction.
On Oct 20, 2023, Tengku Arif Bongsu, together with married couple Nidarahayu and Raibafie, were also charged with 19 counts of money laundering involving more than RM250,000.

For the first to fourth charges, Nidarahayu was accused of disposing of RM20,650.86 in proceeds from unlawful activity from her savings account at CIMB Bank into two other bank accounts at CIMB Bank and Maybank Islamic Bhd's Taman Maluri branch between Sept 15 and Oct 3, 2022.
She also faced 13 charges of transferring RM184,985.46 into the accounts of four companies and eight individuals, also allegedly proceeds from unlawful activity, between Sept 15 and Oct 2 that year.

Raibafie and Tengku Arif Bongsu were respectively charged with receiving RM30,350 and RM25,000 from two bank accounts belonging to Nidarahayu and a company at CIMB Bank's Jalan Bukit Bintang and Taman Mutiara, Cheras branches between Sept 29 and Oct 2, 2022.

The charges were framed under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001, which carries a maximum 15-year jail term and a fine of five times the value of the unlawful activity or RM5 million, whichever is higher, upon conviction.

0eb7e3548f08dc47: NAGOYA, Oct 2 — Japanese judo officials said they had never seen anything like it after eventual champion Rin Maeda appeared to be bitten by her Chinese opponent at the Asian Games.

6796ba0917bc1560: WELLINGTON: World powers are flying delegates to the Pacific to haggle over the fight against global warming, and to see the plight of island nations surrounded by a rising ocean.
Ministers, climate negotiators and a handful of leaders will meet in the Fijian city of Nadi for the Oct 5-8 talks.
They will be charting the course for a major UN-sponsored global climate summit, known as COP31, to be held in November in Turkiye's Antalya province.
For Pacific nations, hosting the preliminary talks in their region offers an opportunity to draw the world's attention to life on the frontline of climate change.
Pacific leaders are pushing for the world to stick to a target of limiting global warming to 1.5C, enhance access to climate finance, and give more attention to the impact on oceans.
The sea level is rising at a record pace, driven by warming oceans and glacier melt, according to a UN report.
Up to 1.2 billion people could be displaced by 2050, with Pacific island countries experiencing sea level rise at twice the global average, said the report released in August.
It also highlighted a financing gap, with developing countries needing US$310-US$365 billion to adapt, yet having only US$26 billion in adaptation finance available in 2023.
Top delegates to the Pacific talks will hold a one-day retreat on low-lying Tuvalu, a small island nation laying plans to relocate the population if it is consumed by the ocean.
They will be shown Tuvalu's land reclamation efforts.
The island capital Funafuti's highest point is just two metres above sea-level, and two of its nine coral atolls are already largely swamped by rising seas.
- 'ACT NOW' -
"Sea-level rise is not a future threat, it is a present reality," Tuvalu Prime Minister Feleti Teo told the UN General Assembly ahead of the climate talks.
"Tuvalu's message is clear: the world must act now decisively, collectively, and with urgency to protect the future for generations to come."
Last year, Australia bowed out of a contest with Turkiye to host the COP31 summit in a deal that let it preside over negotiations and bring the preparatory talks to the Pacific.
As leader of the climate talks, however, major coal exporter Australia has faced heat over the scale of its fossil fuel extraction.
Chris Bowen, the country's climate minister, says Australia is rapidly expanding its renewable energy sources, which are essential for a transition away from fossil fuels.
Bowen, president of the COP31 negotiations, also rejected media criticism that the pre-COP talks in the Pacific had failed to lure enough world leaders.
Fewer than a dozen world leaders have so far publicly confirmed that they will attend the meetings in Fiji and Tuvalu, mostly from the Pacific.
Fiji said last month it expected the heads of state for Antigua and Barbuda, Cape Verde, Thailand, the Maldives and Timor-Leste would attend.
"It's not normally a leaders meeting," Bowen told reporters in the run-up to the talks, which are usually held at the ministerial and senior-negotiator level.
- 'VERY, VERY SAD' -
Organisers have not released detailed figures on attendance.
Bowen said last month 4,000 people from 60 nations would attend, without providing a full breakdown.

Marine scientist Rajneel Singh – part of a team that reported large-scale coral death around Tuvalu from a 2024 marine heatwave – said he was disheartened by a perceived lack of attention to the climate challenge.
"It's very, very sad. There's no awareness of what's happening," Singh told AFP.
Nepal's foreign minister, Shisir Khanal, has confirmed he will attend the Pacific climate meeting, after the August 26 Himalayan flood disaster.
A tsunami-like wall of water and debris triggered by a glacial and rock collapse on the Nepal-China border on August 26 killed nearly 1,500 and left 5,800 missing in the two countries.
"What we're trying to convey to the world is this: these issues of climate change are not theoretical anymore," Khanal told AFP in an interview in New York.--AFP

4ce37412a978dfc4: TAITUNG: Taiwan received on Friday its first F-16V fighter jets made by the United States, as the island democracy upgrades its military capabilities to deter a potential Chinese attack.
The warplanes are part of an US$8 billion deal for 66 F-16Vs approved during US President Donald Trump's first term and scheduled for delivery this year.
The arrival of the aircraft comes as Taiwan awaits Washington's approval of a separate US$14 billion arms package that Trump paused after Chinese objections.
China claims Taiwan is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to seize it.
The two F-16Vs, made by US defence contractor Lockheed Martin, touched down under a clear sky at Taiwan's air force base in Taitung, on the island's southeast coast.
The jets had been expected in early September after making refuelling stops in Hawaii and Guam.
Local media reported that the planes had turned back to Hawaii shortly after taking off for Guam. No official explanation was given.
Dozens of locals, some equipped with binoculars and long-lensed cameras, gathered near the air base's perimeter fence to watch the highly anticipated arrival of the jets.
Kimi Chi, a salesman from the central city of Taichung, had travelled through the night to be able to photograph the aircraft landing in Taitung.
He was philosophical about the delays, saying "good things take time."
"In terms of hardware capabilities, there will definitely be an improvement," the 37-year-old told AFP.
"But what we are actually lacking the most right now is pilots. Of course, I hope the government can provide better additional allowances for these military pilots."

Former Air Force serviceman Eric Chan, 57, marvelled at the improvements made to the F-16 over the past 30 years and said the fighter jets based in Taitung will "play a very important defensive role" against China.
"The threat from the CCP has always been there so we definitely need to strengthen our defence capabilities," Chan told AFP, referring to the Chinese Communist Party.
The F-16V is a fourth-generation multi-role fighter and a significantly upgraded version of Taiwan's ageing F-16 A/B jets.

Equipped with more advanced combat, detection and engine capabilities, the F-16V will be "a valuable addition to Taiwan's air force in countering China's military threat," said Su Tzu-yun, a military expert at the Taipei-based Institute for National Defence and Security Research.
- DELIVERY DELAYS -
The United States is Taiwan's most important security backer and biggest arms supplier. But bottlenecks have slowed delivery of critical weapons.
Taiwan's Defence Minister Wellington Koo said previously it would be "challenging" for all the F-16Vs to be delivered this year, despite Lockheed Martin ramping up production.
On Friday, Koo said more F-16Vs would be delivered to Taiwan "before the end of the year", but did not say how many.
"At present, I think aircraft are gradually moving through the production line, and there are also aircraft that have passed the tests," Koo said.
"As for when they will fly back, we will coordinate further with the US side."

Trump has stalled signing off on the record US$14 billion weapons purchase by Taipei, calling it in May a "very good negotiating chip" in dealings with China, which raised fears that Taiwan's security could be traded away.

Experts believe approval for the package is unlikely before the G20 summit in the United States in December where Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Trump are expected to meet for the fourth time this year.

A US official said recently it was increasingly likely the US$14 billion worth of arms, which include the Patriot air defence system, would be broken up into smaller amounts to temper China's response. --AFP

828c9c94f9f0c87b: TELUK INTAN: Police have uncovered a syndicate offering RM500 to individuals willing to surrender their personal details, including Malaysian passport information, to open Alipay accounts.

b22e8223ef3aa3a5: SEOUL, Oct 2 — South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said today Seoul would take “further measures” if Ukraine refuses to publicly apologise over what he called its unilateral disclosure of North Korean POWs being sent to South Korea.
Seoul has taken a hard stance on Ukraine disclosing the transfer of two soldiers captured fighting for Russia, warning that their families could be targeted by Pyongyang.

The POWs were captured by Ukrainian forces early last year after being deployed alongside thousands of North Korean troops to support Russia’s war against Ukraine, in exchange for economic and military assistance to Pyongyang.

Hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky disclosed last week the transfer in remarks at the United Nations, South Korea’s Lee expressed his dismay, with Seoul claiming confidentiality was key to protecting the POWs’ relatives.

Seoul later demanded an official apology from Ukraine, saying that both sides had reached a “clear understanding” during consultations to keep the transfer confidential — citing concerns for the safety of the POWs’ families in North Korea.
“If Ukraine continues to refuse to acknowledge the facts and publicly apologise, we will take further measures,” said the South Korean President today, accusing Kyiv of making him out to be a “liar”.
“This is a matter concerning the dignity of the Republic of Korea and its people and cannot be overlooked,” Lee posted on X.

Analysts say that from South Korea’s perspective, keeping the transfer of the POWs confidential may have partly been for Ukraine’s sake, as making it public could have complicated Kyiv’s own prisoner exchanges with Russia.

In domestic South Korean politics, however, Seoul’s approach “could prove problematic”, Shin Yul, a political science professor at Myongji University, told AFP, given the current administration’s dovish approach to the nuclear-armed North.

“The government has acted swiftly in this case involving Ukraine, while exercising extreme caution over the North Korean landmine incident (that injured South Korean soldiers). That contrast could leave the public deeply dissatisfied.”
Lee referred today to an interview with Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha published by RBC-Ukraine and other Ukrainian outlets yesterday.
Sybiha said he would “not like to call it an incident”, describing it instead as a “diplomatic misunderstanding”.
“South Korea is an important country for us. And I very much hope for momentum, continued cooperation, and concrete results that we are indeed achieving with them,” he said.
North Korea is known to retaliate against defectors and their families.
Both POWs are identifiable as they had been photographed by South Korean media before their arrival to the South.

Seoul’s spy agency said that Zelensky may have disclosed the transfer of the North Korean soldiers to boost public support in South Korea for Seoul providing arms to Ukraine, a lawmaker said Wednesday.
South Korea has in recent years emerged as a major arms exporter — particularly since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in early 2022 — including through a multibillion-dollar arms deal with Poland.
But it has refrained from supplying Kyiv with lethal weapons, citing its longstanding policy of not arming countries engaged in active conflicts. — AFP
2d854e4b839975f1: PARIS, Oct 2 — Amnesty International said yesterday that Iran must halt any plans to punish a singer and eight other musicians with dozens of lashes each after they livestreamed a performance on YouTube.

The concert featured Parastoo Ahmadi singing powerful, mournful songs to an empty audience, on a dimly-lit stage adorned solely with a large Persian carpet in the grounds of a traditional caravanserai complex.
Ahmadi was backed by a pianist, drummer, guitarist and bassist and all the musicians wore black.
The singer was dressed in a long gown and wore deep red lipstick without adhering to strict Islamic dress code, in a country where women are banned from singing and must cover their hair in public.

A court sentenced the group to 74 lashes each, a sentence that was upheld by an appeals court in the northern province of Qom today, according to the US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) and local media.

“Iranian authorities must immediately halt any plans to carry out floggings, which amount to torture, against singer Parastoo Ahmadi and eight others in connection to a live-streamed 2024 concert in Qom province,” Amnesty said in a statement posted on Instagram.
“Flogging constitutes cruel, inhuman and degrading punishment, and violates the absolute prohibition on torture and other ill-treatment.
“These flogging sentences highlight the inhumanity and brutality of Iran’s justice system and its role in the ongoing assault on women’s rights.”
Ahmadi livestreamed the concert on her own channel in December 2024, where it has been viewed three million times. It has also been viewed many thousands of times more on other channels.

Increasing numbers of Iranian women are appearing without hijab, especially since protests erupted following the death in custody of a woman named Mahsa Amini in September 2022. She had been arrested for allegedly violating the dress code.
Since then, Iran had once again erupted in nationwide protests, peaking in January before the United States and Israel launched a war against the Islamic republic.
Amnesty said Iran must “also abolish compulsory veiling and corporal punishment and end the criminalisation of freedom of expression”. — AFP

a7db5135cb43f6ac: JERUSALEM: Arab Israeli politician Sami Abu Shehadeh withdrew his candidacy on Thursday from October's parliamentary election after Israel's Supreme Court indicated a majority of its judges supported barring him from the race.

Arab Israeli parties are seen by political analysts as potential kingmakers in the Oct 27 election, with polls showing neither prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition nor the main opposition bloc on course for a majority.
Abu Shehadeh leads the left-wing Palestinian Balad party and served in the Knesset, Israel's parliament, from 2019 to 2022.
The Balad leader was withdrawing his candidacy, but the decision did not mark the end of his political struggle, his party said in a statement, adding that he would remain the party's leader.
Last week, Israel's Central Elections Committee voted to disqualify Abu Shehadeh at the request of far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir.
The move came after an article in which Abu Shehadeh described Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack as an "important historical event".
He has denied supporting the attack, but the remarks drew sharp criticism.
The Supreme Court convened on Thursday to hear Abu Shehadeh's appeal against the disqualification.
Rather than issue a ruling, the court proposed that he voluntarily withdraw after signalling that most of its judges favoured excluding him from the election.
It gave him until Friday morning to decide.
Abu Shehadeh had little choice but to withdraw in order to avoid a formal disqualification that would have "grave consequences for the country's political and parliamentary life", Balad said.
'Severe blow'
Disqualifying candidates is rare in Israel, where the Supreme Court has historically overturned most bans approved by the elections committee.

Under Israeli law, candidates can be barred only if they deny Israel's existence as a Jewish and democratic state or support armed struggle by an enemy state or a terrorist organisation against Israel.
Adalah, the Israeli rights group representing Abu Shehadeh, accused the Supreme Court of effectively disqualifying him by pressuring him to withdraw.
"A Palestinian leader has been forced out of the Israeli Knesset elections after the Supreme Court made clear it would remove him," the group said in a statement to AFP.
Adalah said Abu Shehadeh's decades of public life as a human rights activist, legislator and party leader demonstrated his "consistent and unequivocal opposition to violence of any kind".
"It is a severe blow to the right of Palestinian citizens to be represented and to stand for election," it said.
Besides Abu Shehadeh, the elections committee last week barred two Arab electoral lists: the United Arab List and the Joint List, a three-party alliance that includes Balad.
The Supreme Court is due to continue hearing appeals from those parties on Friday.
Arab Israelis, also known as Palestinian citizens of Israel, account for about 20 percent of the country's population. Most identify as Palestinians.
They are descendants of Palestinians who remained within Israel's borders after the state's creation in 1948 and have long complained of discrimination compared with Israel's Jewish majority.

f589eaf786620dcb: BEIJING: An advocacy group and US lawmakers criticised Starbucks for opening its first cafes in China's Xinjiang, where activists and foreign governments have alleged widespread rights abuses against the region's Muslim Uyghur population.

Rights groups say serious abuses continue in the region, including forced labour.
The Chinese government denies the accusations and says its policies have rooted out extremism and brought economic development.
The US has imposed sanctions in response to alleged abuses and several Western brands have faced criticism for connections to Xinjiang.
Last year, French sports retailer Decathlon was accused of purchasing textiles from suppliers that used forced Uyghur labour in the northwestern region.
Decathlon said in response it condemned forced labour and would take action if the allegations were correct.
The Chinese government has invested heavily in Xinjiang - which was one of the country's fastest-growing regions in 2025 - and is promoting a tourism boom.
Last year, Starbucks announced it would sell a controlling stake in its Chinese retail operations to investment firm Boya Capital in the hope of revitalising business in its second-largest market.

c9541d92bbb5903b: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit's appreciation is expected to become more evident in 2027 as Bank Negara Malaysia is projected to raise its overnight policy rate once as part of its monetary policy normalisation, RHB Research said.
Analyst Alexander Chia said Malaysia's stronger growth and export performance should provide the main domestic anchor for the ringgit.

He said the ringgit was expected to strengthen gradually through 2027, supported by stronger economic growth, export earnings and a persistent current account surplus, although a wider US rate advantage is likely to cap gains in the near term.
RHB Research has revised its US dollar/ringgit forecasts to 4.05 by end-2026 and 3.98 by end-2027, pointing to a measured appreciation path rather than a sharp one-way move.

The research house expects the US Federal Reserve to raise its federal funds rate once more in the fourth quarter of 2026, keeping the US-Malaysia interest rate differential elevated through year-end and limiting near-term ringgit gains.

Malaysia's economy expanded 6.0 per cent year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, accelerating from 5.4 per cent in the first quarter, supported by resilient household spending, investment and external demand.

"We forecast Malaysia's economy to grow by 5.4 per cent in 2026 and 4.9 per cent in 2027, which would keep growth comfortably above its pre-pandemic average despite some moderation next year," Chia said in a note.
Export momentum is also supporting the currency, with shipments rising 45.5 per cent year-on-year to RM191 billion in August.

Chia said continued demand for semiconductors, data-processing equipment, electrical and electronics products and data-centre infrastructure should generate foreign-currency receipts and support corporate demand for the ringgit.
Malaysia's electronics trade surplus should also help cushion the impact of a higher energy import bill amid elevated oil prices, he said.
A persistent current account surplus provides a more structural source of support for the currency.
Malaysia recorded an RM10.8 billion current account surplus in the second quarter of 2026, while Bank Negara expects the full-year surplus to remain between 1.5 per cent and 2.5 per cent of GDP.
"Our forecasts place the current account surplus at above 2.2 per cent of GDP in both 2026 and 2027, supported by the goods trade surplus and improving tourism receipts.

"This reduces Malaysia's dependence on external financing and provides an underlying supply of foreign currency when exporters and other resident companies convert their overseas earnings," Chia said.
However, Chia cautioned that a current account surplus does not automatically translate into ringgit appreciation, as some export proceeds may be retained overseas.
Still, he said the surplus should reduce the currency's vulnerability compared with regional economies that rely more heavily on foreign capital to finance external deficits.
US dollar strength, higher US yields and renewed global risk aversion remain key risks to the ringgit outlook.

Chia said stronger-than-expected US economic data, additional Federal Reserve tightening beyond its forecast or a further rise in the US term premium could draw capital towards US dollar assets and trigger foreign outflows from Malaysian Government Securities.

An escalation in Middle East tensions could also weigh on the ringgit, as higher volatility typically increases demand for US dollar liquidity, while the currency remains sensitive to shifts in global risk appetite.

Chia said although Malaysia's energy exports and electronics trade surplus provide some protection, they may not fully offset broader risk-off flows or the domestic cost pressures arising from prolonged high oil prices.
On the fiscal front, higher energy subsidies, weaker tax collection, slower subsidy rationalisation or lower Petronas dividends could make the government's deficit target more difficult to achieve.

Chia said a combination of stronger US dollar demand, foreign outflows from MGS and fiscal deterioration would delay the expected decline in USD/MYR and pose the main downside risk to its 4.05 and 3.98 forecasts.

962b5728d1b8ab0c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Most people spend their 50th year reflecting on the past or settling into a comfortable routine.
But corporate trainer and TEDx speaker Imran Zainal decided to turn the entire Klang Valley into a message to the nation.

In an extraordinary feat of GPS art that spanned 1,230 square kilometres — larger than the landmass of Singapore — Imran spent 12 days driving and walking to trace a massive, legible message across the map: “Happy Msia Day. Create As 1. And Rise.”
While the final image is digital GPS art, the journey to create it was far from smooth.

It was a gruelling, solitary pursuit that saw Imran navigating construction sites, wading through unkempt cemeteries and battling the limitations of map data, all while trying to complete the project in time for Malaysia Day.
The perfectionist’s gamble
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The entire GPS art spans 1,230 square kilometres across Klang Valley, bigger than the landmass of Singapore. — Picture courtesy of Imran Zainal
The project, which ran from August 26 to September 7, was not always meant to be a solo mission.
Imran initially partnered with someone to help record the GPS data, but the collaboration quickly hit a wall due to Imran’s self-described “OCD” levels of perfectionism.
“I would notice a line wasn’t perfect, or a path was slightly off, and I’d need to backtrack and redo it,” Imran said.
His partner, not sharing the same obsession with precision, eventually parted ways with him.
The split cost Imran a month of progress, as the location data was stored on his partner’s device.
With Malaysia Day fast approaching, he was forced to start from scratch, but looking back, he believed the setback allowed him to work without compromise.
“Being on my own meant I could be as meticulous as I needed to be without compromise,” he said.
“It was a massive amount of physical and mental energy for one person, but it felt right. It was a story of unity — but one I had to write alone.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Imran Zainal had to pass through the urban maze of Klang Valley and some dead ends to complete certain letters and shapes. — Picture by Choo Choy May
From thorns to construction sites
The scale of the project required more than just driving.
While 85 per cent of the route was completed by car, the remaining 15 per cent demanded manual, physical labour.
To complete the intricate shapes within the letters – such as the wings of a dove and the delicate petals of a hibiscus flower in Kajang – Imran found himself trekking through overgrown
Chinese cemeteries in Kajang and Klang.
He emerged from these sessions literally “covered in thorns and blood”.
Navigating the urban maze of the Klang Valley presented its own set of hurdles.
In Cheras, a planned route led directly into a construction site.
Refusing to deviate, Imran said he spoke with the safety officer and explained his mission to record the data.
The interaction ended with him donning a construction helmet after being granted special permission to pass through.
“Sometimes, I just had to improvise when I encountered unexpected roadblocks, construction or outdated map data,” he said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The completed GPS art with a message ‘Happy Msia Day. Create As 1. And Rise’. — Picture courtesy of Imran Zainal
Finding the second act
For Imran, the project was about more than national pride; it also brought him back to creative pursuits he had left behind.
Drawing inspiration from 1990s cinema, he recalled how Matt Damon and Ben Affleck wrote Good Will Hunting when they were young, before eventually making their mark in Hollywood.
He, too, had once spent time in Oxford library archives in the late 1990s researching a script, only to eventually abandon his creative pursuits for the predictability of the corporate world.
Turning 50, he began thinking about whether there was a “second act” to his life.
“The people who truly make a difference to our communities are the ones who continuously reinvent themselves,” Imran said. “It doesn’t matter what age you are; you are capable of doing great things.”
A message for the next generation
The artwork concluded at KL Tower, where Imran invited his hiking and life coaching students to join him in finishing the final 50 metres of the letter ‘S’.
He said it was a poignant moment, symbolising the passing of the baton from one generation to the next, with Malaysian, Japanese and Chinese youths participating in a project built around unity.
The “create as 1” message, he explained, is a call for Malaysians to collaborate rather than compete, reflecting what he sees as the spirit of the country’s independence movement.
As for what lies ahead, Imran is already dreaming up his next project: a silhouette of the country’s first prime minister, Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra Al-Haj.
“No matter how my life ends, this will be a feather in my cap,” Imran said.
“At the end of the day, nobody looks back at their life and thinks, ‘I’m so glad I fulfilled my bills.’ You want to be able to say you did something different.”

267674a43be39f5c: MEDICO-LEGAL complaints in Malaysia's public healthcare system have risen in recent years, increasing from 165 cases in 2021 to 283 in 2023.
The upward trend presents opportunities for the healthcare sector to strengthen Malaysia's medical dispute resolution system.

Most are resolved through internal review or ex gratia mechanisms without proceeding to court. Even so, these cases play an important role in shaping clinical practice, communication standards, and how patients experience care.
At the same time, a related challenge lies in the difficulty patients and families face in distinguishing between adverse outcomes and negligence.
Not all unwanted outcomes are the result of wrongdoing, as medicine, by nature, carries inherent risks, and complications can arise even when care meets accepted standards.
In the absence of clear communication, adverse outcomes could be misinterpreted as errors or misconduct. This is an understandable reaction, particularly when outcomes are severe or unexpected.

Having a structured, transparent system, including early explanation, can help bridge this gap in understanding, reducing the likelihood that every adverse outcome is automatically escalated into a legal dispute.
At the same time, Malaysia's medico-legal landscape would benefit from a stronger emphasis on mediation and early resolution before cases proceed to court.

Litigation is often lengthy, costly, and emotionally taxing for all parties involved. Embedding mediation earlier in the process can reduce delays, lower costs, and preserve relationships between patients and healthcare providers.

Another structural issue lies in the role of expert witnesses. In medico-legal proceedings, judges rely heavily on expert testimony to interpret clinical decisions and determine whether standards of care were met.
The quality, objectivity and availability of these experts are central to achieving fair outcomes. We face several challenges in this area.

Unlike some jurisdictions that maintain formal registries of expert witnesses, our system relies largely on ad hoc participation by specialists, often driven by professional goodwill. This creates a limited pool of available experts and contributes to delays, with cases sometimes taking three to five years to conclude.
Reliance on overseas experts as witnesses is not always an ideal solution. Differences in local clinical context and practice environments can limit the relevance of external opinions.

So, we need a structured, locally grounded expert witness system, including formal recognition of expert contributions, safeguards to ensure neutrality, and institutional support that reinforces professional responsibility.
There may also be a natural reluctance among some doctors to testify against peers within a relatively small and closely connected medical community.

A more constructive framing is to view expert involvement as a contribution to system learning and justice. Doctors who serve as expert witnesses must be seen as providing objective clinical interpretation to support fair and informed decisions, not "betraying" their peers.

Ultimately, the effectiveness of any medico-legal system rests on trusted systems and in the fairness of the legal process itself. Plus, early communication, credible mediation pathways, and a robust expert witness framework all contribute to building this trust.
Without these elements, even clinically appropriate outcomes may be perceived as unjust, prolonging disputes and deeper emotional strain for all involved.
Malaysia's medical dispute landscape has reached a point where it needs a more structured and transparent approach, paving the way for a safer healthcare system.
DATUK DR KULJIT SINGH President, Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia

541a2bb315dbb677: Amazon Web Services has debuted an agent that it says will evaluate your cloudy environment “as an experienced cloud architect would” and recommend useful changes. The cloud colossus named its bot the “AWS Well-Architected Agent,” a nod to the Well-Architected Framework that outlines best practices for using the Amazonian cloud. Amazon’s announcement says the agentic incarnation of the Framework analyzes AWS environments “against Well-Architected best practices across 65+ AWS services” and then delivers “targeted, contextual recommendations for improving your applications’ cost, security, performance, and resilience.” “It generates recommendations aligned to your declared business goals, delivers implementation packages with every finding, and surfaces cross-pillar trade-offs making it simpler to remediate the findings,” we’re told. The agent also delivers “ready-to-implement fixes” and “provides individual resource findings with specific dollar impact (where applicable) and step-by-step remediation, consolidated findings across multiple resources scoped to your application, and broad architectural patterns and designs with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) code changes needed to align with Well-Architected best practices.” AWS offers myriad services — some of them with overlapping features and functions. Customers often find themselves using more services than they intended, or using services that aren’t quite right for their intended use. AWS is generally happy if customers change to more appropriate services, even when that sees them spend less, and offers assistance from its own staff or channel partners to make it happen. This agent may make some of that human assistance less necessary. AWS is far from alone in suggesting agents should take on some of the chores that human IT professionals perform today - an approach that’s come to be known as AIOps. When your correspondent chats to IT pros about AIOps, they express distrust on grounds that they cannot be sure agents make valid suggestions and feel following bad advice offered by a machine would indefensible if things go pear-shaped. Vendors I’ve spoken to believe IT pros will first cautiously verify recommendations from AIOps systems, and if they see good results allow agents to take more actions without human oversight - but always with the ability to quickly roll back changes. AWS seems to recognize that users won’t go all-in immediately and therefore offers several manual means to apply recommendations the agent suggests, including the command line interface. For now, the agent is available in the US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), and US West (Oregon) regions, but can handle workloads from any AWS commercial Region. It’s only available for users with an AWS support plan. ®

cb4585224b7f7762: KUALA LUMPUR: Yinson Renewables has secured about NZ$290 million (RM760 million) in financing for its 94.6MW Mt Cass Wind Farm in New Zealand.
The financing package comprises senior construction and term loan facilities, a debt service reserve facility and instrument facilities.
MUFG Bank Ltd led the financing alongside HSBC and Bank of New Zealand, with all three acting as mandated lead arrangers and bookrunners.
MUFG also served as sole structuring coordinator, facility agent and security trustee, while HSBC acted as the account bank.
Yinson Renewables said the financial close represents one of the largest wind project financings completed in New Zealand in recent years.
Construction of the project, located on New Zealand's South Island, began earlier this year, with commercial operations targeted for 2028.
The wind farm is expected to generate enough clean electricity to power about 40,000 homes and contribute to New Zealand's decarbonisation efforts.
Vegard Urnes, chief executive officer of Yinson Renewables, said Mt Cass would be an important addition to the group's renewable energy portfolio.

"Mt Cass is a defining project for Yinson Renewables. As our first wind energy project and our first project in New Zealand to reach financial close, it expands our renewable energy platform and establishes a strong foundation for our continued growth in the market," he said.
"This milestone is the culmination of years of focused development work, and we look forward to delivering a project that will contribute meaningfully to New Zealand's energy transition."
The project also marks Yinson Renewables' first wind energy project and first project in New Zealand to reach financial close.
8c96599ccf7661a0: NAGOYA: Taiwan boxer Lin Yu-ting, the Olympic champion who found herself embroiled in a major gender row at Paris 2024, won gold at the Asian Games on Wednesday.
Lin beat China's Yang Chengyu 5-0 in the women's 60kg final in Nagoya, giving her a second Asian Games gold after winning in the 57kg class in Hangzhou three years ago.
The 30-year-old was backed by a small pocket of vocal Taiwanese supporters in the cosy Nishio Gymnasium.
Towering over her opponent, Lin used her superior reach to take control of the bout and had a clear advantage heading into the third and final round.
She held off a late assault from Yang to take gold, celebrating with the minimum of fuss.
Lin told AFP before the Games that she had considered retiring after the Paris Olympics but wanted to carry on fighting in part to defy those who questioned her eligibility.

Lin and Imane Khelif of Algeria were disqualified from the 2023 world championships by the International Boxing Association (IBA) after the organisation said they failed unspecified gender eligibility tests.
However, the IOC allowed them to compete in Paris, saying they were victims of "a sudden and arbitrary decision" by the widely discredited IBA. Both went on to win gold.
Lin triumphed at 57kg in the French capital but has stepped up a weight division for the Asian Games in Japan.
China's Olympic champion Wu Yu also won gold, defending her Asian Games title in the 51kg class.
Wu beat Vietnam's Nguyen Thi Tam 5-0.

8b0824dadd378fac: TOYOHASHI: Taekwondo dates back more than 2,000 years, but on Friday at the Asian Games the Korean martial art stepped into a not-so-brave future where nobody gets hurt: virtual taekwondo.
At a gymnasium about a 90-minute drive from the main Games host city of Nagoya, a modest number of spectators watched with a mix of fascination and bewilderment.
Taekwondo officials have billed it as "real-world martial arts meets cutting-edge virtual technology."
Competitors wear a VR headset and motion tracking technology allows their movements to control their in-game avatars.
They have "nodes" on their back, thighs and shins to pick up each bodily action.
Rounds are typically 60 seconds each and matches are a best of three rounds, the two combatants standing within their own play area a few metres apart.
The goal is to aim real-life kicks to the virtual body and head of their opponent to deplete their computerised health bar.
The opponent is physically there, standing on an opposing side, but there is never any real-life contact.
Darren Yap won bronze – to go with another bronze in the traditional format.
"It was fun playing out there. I had zero expectations," said the Singaporean.
Asked what he could see through the VR headset, he said: "You can see your health bar, your opponent's character, your limbs.
"It's actually quite nice to wear.
"It's a fun way to do sparring and it's a fun way to do taekwondo without the contact."
- 'Groundbreaking' -
Officials say virtual taekwondo is just as athletically demanding as the real thing, but safer.
Governing body World Taekwondo "proudly endorses" it, calling it "groundbreaking."
Sceptics say it is just another type of gaming.
The first world championships were in 2024 in Singapore, but on Friday it arrived at a bigger stage.
One of the differences to the real-life sport is that men and women compete in a mixed category. There are also no weight classes.
"It allows more people to participate in the sport, and I think it's cool that women are able to beat men," said Yap, 22, after losing his semi-final to Vietnam's woman athlete Chau Ngoc Tuyet Sang.
Singapore has become the early home of the sport. Virtual taekwondo appeared at the inaugural Olympic Esports Week in the city-state in 2023.
Silver medallist Chau, who also competes in the real-life format, had mixed feelings about no gender or weight separation.
"One advantage is that you don't have to worry about the difference in weight," the 21-year-old said.
"But one disadvantage is that men and women can have differences in physical strength, and men may tend to be stronger.
"That could also mean that some of the movements are faster than those performed by women."-AFP

967dd7009ee493d0: PETALING JAYA: A police officer was sentenced to eight years' jail by the Temerloh sessions court in Pahang today for cheating two men of RM111,485 over a three-year period.
Darren anak Ayian was also fined RM44,000 and ordered to be given six strokes of the rotan by judge Jamaludin Mat after he pleaded guilty to 44 charges under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
He was accused of cheating Chong Kin Yew and Yap Kah Poh between December 2022 and March 2025 by claiming that he could help resolve their foreign spouses’ permits with the immigration department.
In handing down the sentence, Jamaludin said Darren had exploited the trust given to him as a police officer.
The court was told that Yap handed over RM76,939 to Darren while Chong gave him RM34,546.
“Both cases showed a repeated modus operandi,” Jamaludin said.
He also said the eight-year sentence was neither excessive nor inadequate.

“Public trust in enforcement officers must be safeguarded, and when such trust is used to facilitate the commission of an offence, deterrence is a factor that needs to be taken into account during sentencing,” he said.
4f93124321a6a9b2: PETALING JAYA: One of the 55 Malaysians who went missing following the glacial floods in Nepal on Aug 26 was found safe and returned to Malaysia this morning.
A group representing the families of the 55 Malaysians said it was informed by Wisma Putra that the man showed up at the Malaysian embassy in Kathmandu yesterday.
Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope, or Masfih, said the Malaysian was travelling alone in Nepal and was at Nagthali on Aug 25, a day before the floods struck.
He was stranded at Nagthali for a period of time due to a loss of communication access and damaged infrastructure, but eventually managed to reach the embassy.
"He returned to Malaysia this morning and is now with his family," Misfah said in a statement.

"If one can be safe, stranded and out of communication for a long period before finally being found and reunited with their family, we do not want to lose hope for the 54 Malaysians who are still uncontactable," it said.
f446ff830f70f4fc: KO LAN: The sea off Thailand's popular tourist island of Ko Lan turned a bright, pungent green this week as heavy rains and floods helped spark a plankton bloom that kept some swimmers on shore.

Dense patches of green could be seen stretching along parts of the coast, with jet skis floating in discoloured waters around the island in the northern part of the Gulf of Thailand, while other stretches of the shoreline were unaffected.

"What we're actually seeing with the naked eye is a colour that comes from a type of plankton called Noctiluca," said Arvut Munhapon, a senior researcher and head of marine environmental research at the Marine Science Research Division, Institute of Marine Science, Burapha University.

His team of four was on the ground collecting water samples, measuring water quality, and bringing samples back to the lab to identify species and build a database that would help form a clearer picture of the situation.
"Plankton blooms are a natural, recurring phenomenon, but have worsened around the world as climate change has warmed seas," the researchers said.
"Fertiliser runoff and nutrient-rich wastewater also wash into the sea and feed rapid plankton growth," they said.

Blooms typically last two to three days. When they end, mass plankton die-off consumes oxygen and sometimes creates hypoxic conditions, or an "aquatic dead zone", with oxygen levels too low to support marine life, according to Anukul Buranapratheprat, deputy director of the Institute of Marine Science, Burapha University.
"We're looking at the endpoint, which is hypoxia ... and hypoxia in the inner Gulf of Thailand, based on my own research, has genuinely gotten more severe," Anukul said.
His biggest concern was a wide hypoxic zone that had formed this year, too low in oxygen to support bottom-dwelling marine life.

This year's monsoons and El Niño may be intensifying both the bloom and this year's hypoxic conditions, since warmer water holds less dissolved oxygen, but Anukul said more research was needed to confirm the connection.
Significant flooding has hit Thailand in recent weeks, including in central provinces and Bangkok, adding to the volume of freshwater reaching the Gulf.
Food vendors along the beach said customer numbers had thinned since the green water appeared, with some visitors moving to unaffected areas of the island.
The discolouration was enough to keep others out of the sea altogether.

"I felt that it was unusually green compared to normal seawater, so I didn't dare go in. I was afraid I'd break out in a rash,” Latipeya Thantibhapat, a 29-year-old tourist from Chiang Mai, told Reuters.
c80f5159fcd794bb: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The 2026 Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix, which Malaysia is hosting this weekend, will be broadcast live on RTM, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.
